title: Session-safe eviction + background compactor to stabilize GPU OOMs under KV pressure
creator: Ava Patel
description: High-severity customer escalations across Hosted/Dedicated/Private revealed a correlated failure mode: long-lived sessions holding KV handles plus allocator slab fragmentation cause sustained GPU memory pressure and intermittent OOMs. This ticket implements a runtime fix: a session-safe eviction protocol that atomically demotes unused KV entries, plus a low-priority background compaction pass and allocator high-water triggers to proactively reclaim fragmented arenas.
problem_summary: Multiple customers reported GPU OOMs during prolonged chat sessions and batch jobs. Root cause analysis shows KV cache reference pinning, uneven arena slab utilization, and lack of incremental compaction causing large unreclaimable fragments. Symptoms: sudden OOMs with high free fragmentation, session-specific memory spikes, and reproduction under synthetic long-tail workloads.
root_cause: 1) KV handles stayed pinned by session-level references (edge-case in session GC). 2) Allocator fragmentation + tensor arena alignment led to unreclaimable slabs. 3) No background compaction to defragment between requests. Together these amplified under dedicated GPU pool pressure.
solution_summary: Introduce three complementary runtime changes: 1) session-safe eviction token to allow in-flight sessions to release inactive KV entries without invalidating active cursors; 2) background compactor that scans low-priority arenas and coalesces free spans; 3) allocator high-water threshold with conservative early eviction and a metrics-based circuit-breaker to avoid cascading OOMs. Also add telemetry and debug endpoints for live inspection.
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: - Background compaction runs at low priority to avoid disrupting latency-critical inference; trades CPU for lower OOM risk. - Eviction token allows safe reclamation but requires additional reference counting complexity. - Conservative thresholds chosen to minimize false positives for eviction at cost of additional memory overhead (+5-8% observed in staging).
implementation_notes: - New runtime flag --evict-token-lease-ms and --compactor-interval-ms. - Compactor uses asynchronous GPU-to-CPU copies for span analysis to avoid blocking kernels. - Added metrics: kv_pinned_handles, arena_free_frag_pct, compactor_runs, evict_token_reclaims. - Unit tests for handle race, canary perf test harness for synthetic long-tail sessions.
qa_and_testing: - Reproduced locally with long-session harness (script: scripts/repro/kv_stress_long_session.sh). - Staging canaries run on both Dedicated and Private clusters with 48h soak. - Perf regression threshold: median latency +3% and p99 +10%; these were within acceptable SLO for canary. - Added chaos tests: intermittent network stalls to ensure safe eviction under partial failures.
deployment_plan: 1) Merge PR and land runtime-1.22-canary images. 2) Deploy to a small set of Dedicated pools and two Private customer clusters for 72h. 3) Monitor metrics and error budgets. 4) If stable, rollout to non-paying Hosted nodes with traffic shaping; enable on-hosted gradually. 5) If issues, rollback via runtime rollback pipeline. Coordinated with SRE and Customer Success for escalated customers.
canary_results: Dedicated canary: no OOMs after 72h, arena_free_frag_pct reduced from median 28% -> 9%. Private canary: one transient reclaim spike resolved automatically. Hosted limited rollout: observed slight increase in scheduling latency (median +2.1%).
postmortem_followups: Create retro doc and link to postmortem (CON-INV-426).
Add more fine-grained per-session KV TTLs in console as opt-in.
Explore allocator redesign for next quarter to reduce fragmentation at source.
